lesson.title: Quick Facts: 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s and 10s

steps.say: You already know your twos, fives and tens like the back of your hand. Today we add the threes and fours to that club, so all five of these times tables come out fast, without counting on your fingers.

visual.caption: The four times table on the hundred chart: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40

steps.say: Here is the trick for the fours. Fours are just doubles of doubles. To find four times seven, first double seven to get fourteen, then double fourteen to get twenty-eight. So four times seven is twenty-eight.

visual.caption: Four groups of seven: two groups make 14, and 14 doubled is 28

steps.say: And here is the trick for the threes. A three is just a double plus one more group. To find three times eight, double eight to get sixteen, then add one more eight to get twenty-four. So three times eight is twenty-four.

visual.caption: Three groups of eight: 8 and 8 makes 16, plus one more 8 makes 24

steps.say: Let us try a real one. Granola bars at the store cost four dollars a box, and your mum buys six boxes for soccer snacks. Double six is twelve, and double twelve is twenty-four. Six boxes cost twenty-four dollars.

visual.caption: Six boxes at four dollars each: 24 dollars in all

steps.say: Watch out for one slip that trips lots of kids up. For three times eight, some people double eight and then double it again and say thirty-two. But that is four eights, not three! For threes you double and then add just one more group: sixteen plus eight is twenty-four.

visual.caption: The three times table lands on 24, never on 32

steps.say: So remember: for fours, double and double again. For threes, double and add one more group. Your twos, fives and tens are already quick, and now the threes and fours can be too.

lesson.answer: Fours are double-double; threes are double plus one more group.

practice.question: A pack of maple cookies costs three dollars at the Vancouver bake sale. Kavya buys seven packs. How much does she pay? Try the doubling trick: double seven, then add one more seven.
practice.answer: Twenty-one dollars. Double seven is fourteen, and fourteen plus seven is twenty-one, so three times seven is twenty-one.
